source.title: Perspective: A Phase Diagram for Deep Learning unifying Jamming, Feature Learning and Lazy Training
source.authors: M. Geiger; Leonardo Petrini; M. Wyart

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own width sweeps and test-error curves bearing on model-wise double descent, using a specific empirical setup and also examining ensemble averages.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error curves against width in Fig. 5 and an output-fluctuation measurement in Fig. 7D. Fig. 7A varies training-set size but shows the zero-training-loss boundary, not test error against sample size. Epoch-wise curves are not reported. Results from cited studies, including the stripe-model curves, are not extracted as this paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The paper presents new width sweeps (Fig. 4, Fig. 5) of fully connected two-hidden-layer nets on binary, PCA-reduced MNIST and CIFAR10. Individual-net test error peaks at the jamming (zero-training-loss) transition and then falls. The ensemble-averaged predictor shows no second descent. This is a different setup from the originals (hinge-loss classification, gradient flow, varied initialization scale) aimed at model-wise double descent and its variance origin.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report that test error peaks (a cusp) at the jamming transition and improves beyond it, independent of initialization scale. They argue, partly from cited prior work [61], that the second descent comes from initialization-induced finite-width fluctuations. Ensemble averaging removes the double descent, and optimal performance comes from ensembling nets of limited width past jamming.
record.recipe_differences: The paper sweeps width and measures test error, but reports fully connected networks with two hidden layers, binary MNIST/CIFAR10 tasks, PCA-reduced inputs, and reduced training sets; it also compares individual predictors with ensemble averages.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error curve is described as showing double descent independently of the tested initialization scale. The paper also reports that ensemble averaging removes the curve.
record.problems: The test-error values are presented in plots and are not extractable from the supplied text. The reported experiments use reduced binary classification tasks and PCA-projected inputs; no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Fig. 7A's sample-size sweep reports the boundary where training loss reaches zero rather than test error, so it does not provide a result for V3.

untested.parts: Only fully connected two-hidden-layer nets on reduced binary MNIST/CIFAR10 with PCA inputs were tested; no CNNs, ResNets, transformers or multi-class tasks.
Label noise, multiple or triple peaks, and optimally tuned regularization are not tested with the paper's own data. The regularization remarks cite [59].

missing.what: Ensemble test error over the (h, α̃) plane (15-net averages) varies only weakly with h once past jamming, at fixed α̃. The jamming position also shifts with α̃ and with allowed run time.

record.verdict_notes: This is a perspective/review article; much of its content is cited results (Figs. 7–10). Only Figs. 4–5 are new data. No uncertainties are given and values are figure-only. The cusp is attributed to divergence of the predictor norm near jamming.

versions.untested_parts: The reported tests use fully connected networks on binary MNIST and CIFAR10 tasks in the stated reduced-data settings; other architectures and settings are not tested here.
The paper examines finite-width initialization fluctuations and ensemble averaging. It does not test label noise, multiple or triple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
